gh pr comment 1398 --body "All four findings addressed. The first was a genuine hole and the way I initially tried to test it is worth recording.

1. **The guard was bypassable.** Correct, and exactly as described: \`previous\` came from an unlocked \`session.get\` before the \`FOR UPDATE\` snapshot, so a stale read skipped the check entirely and could leave **zero stored admins** — the same read-modify-write race the lock exists for, relocated onto \`target.role\`. It also made the audit line's \`previous_role\` wrong. Now the target row is locked first, then the admin set (one consistent order, so these callers cannot deadlock), and membership is read as \`target.id in admin_ids\` so the guard and the count can never drift apart again.

   **My first regression test for it proved nothing.** It drove the three sessions sequentially, which passed against the buggy code too — I only found that out by mutation-checking it. The version that ships exploits the fact that \`session.get\` answers from the identity map with *no round trip*, which makes the stale read deterministic rather than a timing accident, and it is verified to fail against the pre-fix code.

2. **Self-demotion left \`/me\` stale** — right, and the consequence is nasty: the Admin nav and page keep rendering while every action 403s against a UI still insisting you're an admin. Now refetches \`/me\` on a self-change. Refetch rather than a local patch, because \`/me\` reports the *effective* role and an admin still on \`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS\` remains one — only the server knows. Mutation-verified.

3. **Bare \`StopIteration\` → 500, plus a whole-workspace aggregate for one row.** Both fixed with \`get_admin_user\`, which shares one row-builder with \`list_all_users\` so the two cannot disagree about what a row contains, and raises a typed 404.

4. **Dev-bypass refusal preceded the idempotency short-circuit**, contradicting the no-op rule ten lines below. Reordered; covered.

Separately, both new Playwright specs failed CI on locators. Rather than push another guess I stood up **CI's exact lane locally** (dev-bypass api on a scratch database + its own Vite): the migration applied clean against real Postgres, \`PATCH …/role\` demoted and restored a real user, the dev-bypass refusal returned a real 409 with its reason, and all 4 specs pass in a real browser with the workspace left re-runnable. The two traps were an email appearing in three stacked tables (the row matched had no select at all) and antd tagging every select's *current* selection with \`title=<role>\`.

content.content:
# Browser E2E (Playwright)

Drives the **real app in a browser** under dev-bypass auth against the seeded
demo dataset — the other half of the full-stack smoke (#128). The httpx API
smoke (`backend/scripts/e2e_smoke.py`) proves `HTTP → service → DB`; this proves
the React UI a user actually clicks: `browser → Vite proxy → api → DB`.

> Live `test()`/runs against real Snowflake/S3/etc. stay out of scope (no creds
> locally — the documented deferred smoke). The connectivity tests here
> **fail-soft**; the specs assert the health/error path renders, not that a real
> datasource is reachable.

## Specs

| Spec                       | Covers                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smoke.spec.ts`            | dev-bypass auth, app shell, sider nav                                                        |
| `connections.spec.ts`      | seeded connections grouped by type, "Test all" health path                                   |
| `suites.spec.ts`           | seeded suite → checks; check + suite authoring round-trips                                   |
| `results.spec.ts`          | seeded runs, run-detail drill-down, pipeline-runs feed                                       |
| `schedules.spec.ts`        | SchedulesPanel: add / pause / delete + invalid-cron 422 path                                 |
| `trigger-bindings.spec.ts` | TriggersPanel: bind pipeline / disable / remove (seeded ADF connection)                      |
| `notifications.spec.ts`    | NotificationsPanel: threshold routing persisted across reload; write-only webhook affordance |

antd Select gotchas (learned per spec, reuse these): rc-select pre-highlights
option 0 when nothing is selected, so `Enter` alone takes the first option and
`ArrowDown`+`Enter` takes the **second**; option nodes live in an off-viewport
rc-virtual-list measurement container, so `getByRole('option').click()` is
flaky — prefer keyboard navigation with the arrow-delta computed from the
currently rendered value (see `notifications.spec.ts`).

## Run it locally

1. Bring up the stack and seed the demo data:

   ```bash
   docker compose up -d            # postgres + redis + api + worker + frontend
   conda run -n dataq python -m backend.scripts.seed_dev
   ```

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("backend/scripts/seed_dev.py")
s = p.read_text()

helper = '''
# ── Role fixtures for the per-role browser E2E (ADR 0033, #743) ──────────────

#: Where the minted tokens land. Gitignored, regenerated on every seed, and
#: scoped to a throwaway dev/CI database — the same discipline `setup.sh` uses
#: for `.env`: a credential may be *generated* into an untracked file, never
#: committed to one.
ROLE_TOKENS_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "frontend" / "e2e" / ".role-tokens.json"

#: One seeded user per non-admin tier. The dev-bypass identity is always an
#: admin (#741) and cannot be demoted, so a browser cannot experience the other
#: two tiers as itself — these exist so the per-role specs drive a REAL session
#: at a REAL role, rather than mocking `/me` and testing the UI against a lie.
_ROLE_FIXTURES = (
    ("member", "role-member@dataq.local", "Mia Member"),
    ("viewer", "role-viewer@dataq.local", "Vic Viewer"),
)


def _seed_role_fixtures(session: Session, *, owner: User) -> int:
    """Provision a member + a viewer, share a suite with each, and mint a PAT.

    The PAT is the seam that makes this possible at all: `get_current_user`
    resolves a `dq_live_` bearer BEFORE the dev-bypass branch, so a Playwright
    context that sets an Authorization header is that user for every request —
    including the ones the Vite proxy forwards.

    Each fixture gets a `view` share on one suite so their read-only pages have
    something in them; an empty page cannot distinguish "read-only" from
    "broken". `view`, not `edit`, for the viewer specifically — the backend
    rejects `edit` to a viewer (ADR 0033), which is itself the behaviour #741
    tests.
    """
    tokens: dict[str, str] = {}

Two orthogonal axes (ADR [0033](adr/0033-workspace-roles-rbac.md)). Your **workspace

may touch. Neither replaces the other — a Member with no share on a suite still cannot see
it. Both are enforced server-side on REST **and** MCP, and both resolve **per request**, so
a role change takes effect on the target's next call, including calls made with API tokens
they already hold.

| Capability | Admin | Member | Viewer |
|---|---|---|---|
| See/use suites shared to them | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (view only) |
| Create/import suites (become owner) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |

| Manage roles in-app | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

seed and lockout break-glass**: it grants Admin but never removes it, and a role change must

import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("backend/tests/api/test_users.py")
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('''def test_summary_omits_sensitive_fields(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    _user(db_session, "alice@acme.io", display_name="Alice")
    db_session.commit()
    resp = client.get("/api/v1/users/search", params={"q": "alice"})
    [row] = resp.json()
    assert set(row) == {"id", "email", "display_name"}
    assert "aad_object_id" not in row''',
'''def test_summary_omits_sensitive_fields(client: TestClient, db_session: Any) -> None:
    """An EXHAUSTIVE allowlist, deliberately — this directory is readable by every
    authenticated user, so a field must never arrive here by accident. Equality
    (not a subset check) is what makes a new column a failing test rather than a
    silent widening.

    `role` was added in #743 as a considered widening: the share picker has to
    know whether a candidate is a Viewer, or it offers `edit` levels the backend
    (ADR 0033) will refuse. It is coarse workspace metadata of the same kind as
    the email and display name already here — not a credential, not a per-suite
    grant, and not an identity key. `aad_object_id` in particular stays out.
    """
    _user(db_session, "alice@acme.io", display_name="Alice")
    db_session.commit()
    resp = client.get("/api/v1/users/search", params={"q": "alice"})
    [row] = resp.json()
    assert set(row) == {"id", "email", "display_name", "role"}
    assert "aad_object_id" not in row


def test_summary_reports_the_effective_role(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any, monkeypatch: Any
) -> None:
    """The EFFECTIVE role, not the stored column — because that is what
    `share_service` checks when it rejects an `edit` grant. A break-glass
    allowlist admin whose row still reads `member` can hold `edit`, and a picker
    reading the stored value would wrongly refuse them."""
    from backend.app.core.config import get_settings

    user = _user(db_session, "ada@acme.io", display_name="Ada")
    user.role = "member"
    db_session.commit()
    monkeypatch.setenv("WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", "ada@acme.io")
    get_settings.cache_clear()

    [row] = client.get("/api/v1/users/search", params={"q": "ada"}).json()
    assert row["role"] == "admin"''')
p.write_text(s)
PYEOF

## Summary

- The UI now mirrors what the server will actually allow: connections are read-only for non-admins, Viewers get a genuinely read-only shell, and the share picker stops offering `edit` to grantees who cannot hold it.
- **Every gate here is presentation.** #741 re-enforces each one with a 403. The reason to hide a control anyway is honesty — offering an action that will be refused is a worse experience than not offering it.
- Three per-role Playwright specs that authenticate as **real users at real roles**, not mocked ones.

## Linked issue

Refs #743. Refs #744.

## Type of change

- [x] feat — new functionality

## What's gated

| Surface | Admin | Member | Viewer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Add connection · per-card actions menu (edit/re-auth/delete) | ✅ | hidden | hidden |
| Test / Test all | ✅ | ✅ | hidden |
| Connections list + detail | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| New suite · Import | ✅ | ✅ | hidden |
| Offered `edit` in the share picker | ✅ | ✅ | not offered |

Hidden, not disabled — a disabled primary button invites a hunt for the precondition that would enable it, and there isn't one. The per-card actions menu is removed entirely rather than opening to an empty dropdown, since a trigger that opens to nothing reads as *broken*, not *withheld*. Non-admins get a short read-only hint so the missing buttons read as intentional.

## Three decisions worth reviewing

**1. `null` is a real third state.** `useWorkspaceRole()` returns `null` until `/me` resolves, and the capability hooks return `false` during it. A read-only shell that pops controls in mid-fetch is worse than a beat of nothing, and rendering them optimistically is worse still. Asserted in both directions.

**2. The hooks read the EFFECTIVE role.** A break-glass allowlist admin whose stored row still says `member` sees the admin surface — matching what every endpoint will actually do.

**3. The share picker needed a backend change.** To mirror #741's "no `edit` to a Viewer" rejection, the picker has to know the candidate's role, so `UserSummary` now carries it. That is a **considered widening** of an endpoint readable by every authenticated user, and it is recorded in the exhaustive-allowlist test that guards it: the assertion stays an equality check (so a future accidental field still fails), `aad_object_id` still stays out, and the reasoning is in the test's docstring. A role is coarse workspace metadata of the same kind as the email already there — not a credential, not a per-suite grant.

## The per-role E2E authenticate as real users

The dev-bypass identity is always an admin and **cannot be demoted** (#742), so a browser cannot experience the other two tiers as itself. The specs instead set an `Authorization` header with a PAT for a seeded member/viewer — `get_current_user` resolves a `dq_live_` bearer *before* the dev-bypass branch, so the context genuinely *is* that user for every proxied request.

That matters more than convenience: **mocking `/me` would have tested the UI against a lie.** It could not catch a control that is hidden correctly but whose endpoint is ungated, nor a page that 403s for a tier the UI happily renders. Here the server is genuinely deciding.

`seed_dev` mints those tokens into a **gitignored** file (generated, never committed — the same discipline `setup.sh` uses for `.env`), and the specs **skip with an explanatory message** if it is absent: a missing seed is an environment problem, and a red suite that means "you forgot to seed" trains people to ignore red suites.

git add -A && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fixup: address /code-review findings on the role-aware frontend

1. THE VIEWER EDIT-CLAMP WAS DEFEATABLE, and my first regression test
   for it proved nothing. The clamp was re-derived from the transient
   `options` array, so: pick a member → set `edit` → pick a viewer
   (clamps) → search again → the picked user leaves `options`, the
   lookup goes undefined, the Select re-enables at the still-live
   `edit`, and Add POSTs `edit` for the still-selected viewer — the
   exact 422 this mirror exists to avoid. The picked user is now held in
   state.

   My first test skipped the "set edit" step, so the permission was
   `view` throughout and there was nothing for the un-clamp to leak — it
   passed against the buggy code, which I only learned by
   mutation-checking it. Second time this session; the habit earns its
   keep.

2. Hiding the button is not gating the route. `/connections/new`,
   `/connections/:id/edit` and `/suites/new` are deep-linkable, so a
   bookmark, a Back after a demotion, or a shared link reached them
   directly and a Member would fill an entire connection form —
   credential and all — to learn at submit that it 403s. New
   `RequireRole` route guard renders the same honest Forbidden state
   `/admin` uses. `null` renders a spinner, never Forbidden: flashing a
   denial at someone who turns out to be an admin is worse.

3. `seed_dev` picked the shared suite with an unordered `.first()`,
   while `roles.spec.ts` names the suite it expects — heap order moves
   on re-seed, so the viewer's share could land elsewhere and fail the
   spec as if the UI had regressed. Now ordered. Verified by seeding a
   real database three times.

4. It also minted a fresh 90-day PAT per role on every seed and never
   revoked the old one, so keys — and every stale copy of the tokens
   file — accumulated as live credentials, in the one function whose
   whole point is idempotency. Prior keys are now revoked first;
   verified as exactly one live key per fixture after three seeds.

5. `connections.py`'s module docstring still said draft-test was
   MemberUser, contradicting both the code and the feature matrix.
